title: Man. Post. Cap. X: PLAC — prove OT faithful knew antecedent imputation; Scripture? tradition?
pass_a_gloss: Placeus asks the source: how does the learned man know OT faithful knew both equally? From Scripture—why no text? From unwritten tradition—then Scripture was not enough, and where is that tradition? Fleeing to Paul fails: whether Paul taught antecedent imputation is the very dispute; the opponent has not proved he did; Placeus has already proved he did not, and will prove further.
pass_b_english: PLAC. First, from where does the learned man have it that both were equally known to the faithful of the Old Testament?
From Scripture? Why did he not produce a place?
From unwritten tradition? Then Scripture was not enough for them; and where is that tradition?

He flees to Paul in vain: for whether Paul taught that antecedent imputation or not is just what is now disputed between us; the learned man has not proved that he taught it; I have already proved by several arguments that he did not, and I am engaged in proving it.
source_text: PLAC. Primum unde habet Vir doctus fidelibus veteris Testamenti aeque notum utrumque fuisse? Ex Scriptura? Cur locum non protulit? Ex traditione non scripta? Non igitur sufficiebat illis Scriptura; & ubi illa traditio? Ad Paulum frustra confugit: utrum enim illam imputationem antecedentem docuerit, necne, nunc quidem inter nos controvertitur; docuisse non probavit Vir doctus; Ego non docuisse iam aliquot argumentis probavi, & in eo sum ut probem.

choices.choice: No Scripture/tradition proof OT knew antecedent imputation
